structure:
Part 14 of 16, 'ins e2e: the INS front door, dashboard and notification type'. Read in full, at HEAD c293b056f39efb206c6c4f2df54c38e5febd8485: the five flat specs under tests/ins/e2e/features (notification-dashboard-navigation.spec.ts, organisation-scoped-dashboard.spec.ts, aggregated-notification.spec.ts, page-titles.spec.ts, cross-service-sessions.spec.ts) and tests/ins/e2e/features/notification-type/notification-type.spec.ts; the page objects page-objects/ins/dashboard-page.ts, page-objects/ins/notification-type-page.ts, page-objects/ins/index.ts, page-objects/shared/base-page.ts, page-objects/shared/dashboard-copy.ts, page-objects/shared/sets.ts, page-objects/shared/layout-checks.ts, page-objects/shared/opens-at-expected-url.ts, page-objects/shared/auth/sign-in-page.ts, page-objects/shared/auth/organisation-picker-page.ts and page-objects/animals/dashboard-page.ts; the domain files domain/ins/constants/notification-types.ts, domain/ins/constants/dashboard-sort-values.ts and domain/ins/models/db/aggregated-notification-document.ts; flows/ins/journey.ts and flows/shared/journey-context.ts; fixtures/ui.ts and fixtures/auth-state.ts; config/service-base-urls.ts and config/users.ts. For accuracy on what the specs drive, three out-of-slice files were also consulted and are cited only where a claim rests on them: adapters/http/ins-notification-api-client.ts, adapters/http/organisation.ts and the four INS hand-over methods in flows/animals/journey.ts (lines 179-200), plus the two date formatters in utils/date-utils.ts (lines 157-179).

The slice is laid out as six specs in four describe-blocked areas. The INS home and dashboard: one spec proves a submitted notification reaches the INS dashboard and its View link opens the notification in the owning journey frontend; one proves the dashboard list is organisation-scoped through the INS backend's own notification list; one (compose and Mongo only) proves the aggregated notification document the dashboard reads is created at draft and updated in place on submit. The notification-type question: one spec, in three describe blocks, covering the question's own content and validation, the hand-over to the animals and plants services for each of the four options, the Create new button on the INS home, and the round trip back to the question from a started animals draft. Page titles: one spec of nine titles across the INS home, the address book pages and a missing page. Cross-service sessions: one spec proving one browser holds the animals, INS and plants sessions at once.

Test declarations actually present at this commit: notification-type.spec.ts 12 declarations (14 tests at run time, because one is generated in a loop over the three plants options), page-titles.spec.ts 9, and 1 each in aggregated-notification.spec.ts, cross-service-sessions.spec.ts, notification-dashboard-navigation.spec.ts and organisation-scoped-dashboard.spec.ts: 25 declarations, 27 tests at run time. The partition's 'covers' counts (23, 10, 4, 4, 3 and 3) do not match the files as they stand; every test present is claimed here, by its title. Covered as gaps: the dashboard sort control and its four sort labels, the dashboard results label and empty state, the aggregated read model's sort order, signing out of one service, and the absence of a germinal products option. The address book's own behaviour (parts 12 and 13), the transporter, a11y and security specs (part 15) are out of this slice; the address book page titles are claimed here because the page-titles spec is in this slice.

claims.note: mechanism: the suite's own sign-in retry, over the sign-in error page's 'try again' link.

claims.statement: The identity the INS specs sign in as is the trader Andrew Farmer, user ID 2100010101, email test.user11@defra.gov.uk, of organisation 5900001.
claims.note: The file's own words: 'Defra ID stub identities used by the suite. CRNs and organisations mirror trade-imports-defra-id-stub mock data.' The sign-in password is held in an environment variable with a local default [REDACTED].

claims.statement: A signed-in INS session is proven by landing on the address book, not on the dashboard: the address book list is the INS service's checked landing page.
claims.note: mechanism: the worker's saved sign-in state, minted once per domain per worker and reused. The animals and plants services both land on '/'.

claims.statement: Only the session cookie is carried between a worker's tests: the journey state cookie is dropped, so each test starts with a signed-in user and no part-answered notification.
claims.quote: /** The yar `session` cookie carries per-user journey state that would bleed across a worker's tests. */
claims.note: mechanism: the suite's own session reuse, not service behaviour.

claims.statement: Every INS page carries the same service navigation: Home, About, Address book and Dashboard links, the signed-in user's email, and a 'Log out' link.
claims.note: Follows because the shared base page every INS page extends exposes these as page-wide controls; of them, only the Dashboard link is asserted by a test in this slice (repo-tests-p14-054).

claims.statement: The INS home offers a 'Sort by' choice applied with an 'Update sort' button.
claims.note: Follows from the INS dashboard page object; no test in this slice selects a sort. See the gap repo-tests-p14-092.

claims.statement: The INS home's sort choices are 'Arrival date (newest first)', 'Arrival date (oldest first)', 'Last updated (newest first)' and 'Last updated (oldest first)'.
claims.note: These are the labels the suite's sortBy helper selects by; no test in this slice uses any of them.

claims.statement: The INS home shows a count or range label for its results, and a separate message when a search finds nothing.
claims.note: Follows from the two locators the INS dashboard page object exposes ('dashboard-no-results' and 'dashboard-results-label'); neither the wording of the label nor the empty-state message is asserted anywhere in this slice. See the gap repo-tests-p14-092.

claims.statement: No test proves the INS home's sort order, its results count label or its empty state, so the suite holds the service to nothing about any of them.
claims.note: Looked in all five flat specs under tests/ins/e2e/features and in the notification-type spec: none references dropdownSort, sortBy, btnUpdateSort, resultsLabel or noSearchResults, and dashboardSortValues is imported only as a type by the dashboard page object.

claims.statement: No test proves the order the INS home lists notifications in, nor how it orders the aggregated notifications it reads.
claims.note: Both specs work with one notification, found by searching for its own reference; neither creates two and compares their order. The aggregated document carries both an arrival date and a last-updated time, which the sort labels in repo-tests-p14-090 name, but nothing asserts an ordering.

claims.statement: No test proves what signing out of one service does to the user's sessions with the others.
claims.note: The cross-service spec proves only that three sessions can be held at once; it never uses the 'Log out' link the shared base page exposes. Looked in all six specs of this slice for linkSignOut and for 'Log out': no match.

claims.statement: The notification-type question offers no germinal products choice, although the services' set bases name a '/germinal-products' set.
claims.quote: export const NOTIFICATION_TYPE_OPTIONS = [LIVE_ANIMALS, PLANTS_FOR_PLANTING, POTATOES, WOOD_PRODUCTS] as const;
claims.note: Follows because the question's options are asserted to be exactly these four (notification-type.spec.ts:27), while the suite's set bases list germinalProducts: '/germinal-products' as a third set. The suite therefore holds the question to having no germinal products option today.

claims.statement: A journey that crosses from the INS into a service and back takes longer than an ordinary page assertion, and is run with a raised time budget.
claims.quote: test.slow();
claims.note: Every test in this slice that signs in to more than one service, or waits for the aggregated read model, is marked slow; the question's own content and validation tests are not.

claims.statement: A test records the reference numbers of every notification it creates, and they are reported with the test's own result.
claims.note: mechanism: the suite's own diagnostics over the notifications a test created; `journeyContext.referenceNumber` is the most recent one, which the dashboard and organisation-scoping specs read.

claims.statement: The INS address book journey reaches the address type question, the add form and the transporter forms without searching the pages for a route: a type is chosen, then the page it leads to opens.
claims.quote:
/** Chooses a type on the address type page and lands on the page it leads to: the add form for the
   * three types that group roles, or the transporter type question for Transporter. */
claims.note: Read as context for the page-titles spec, which uses toAddressType and toAddressForm. The address book's own behaviour belongs to parts 12, 13 and 15.

claims.statement: Each service the suite drives is addressed by its own base URL, given to the run rather than built into it, and a missing one stops the run with a message naming the setting.
claims.quote: throw new Error(`${envVar} is not set. Ensure Playwright config applies project base URLs before running tests.`);
claims.note: The four front ends named are the animals frontend, the animals admin, the INS frontend and the plants frontend; the INS backend, address book, reference data, Mongo and SQS are addressed the same way.

claims.statement: A notification opened from the INS home is identified only by its reference number: that is the one value that carries from the INS list into the owning service.
claims.quote: const referenceNumber = journeyContext.referenceNumber;
claims.note: Follows because the reference is what the test searches by, what the View link's name and target carry, and what the notification's own page shows back.
